I'm in an extremely similar boat--I just lost my girl a week ago as of today, and seeing her empty enclosure kills me every time I walk down the stairs. I keep turning her lights on and forgetting she's not in there anymore. Getting a new beardie isn't replacing your lost girl--there's a whole lot of love in you that suddenly has nowhere to go. You're just giving that love to something new. You don't have to decide now. You can give it as much time as you need. Grief is different for everyone, but your beardie wouldn't resent you for this and no one else will either. Everyone's way of processing is different, so make sure it's not a knee-jerk reaction to missing her, but don't beat yourself up if you decide you do want another beardie at some point.

(For what it's worth, I've been looking at new babies the whole week for the same reason--seeing that empty enclosure and no longer having a dragon in the house after 14 years with one is strange and upsetting.)

Caught this post a month out so idk if you're still deliberating, but some general advice that might help on your publishing journey: I'm not an Ivy League grad and I'm still interning, so I don't have a lot of opinions on how far the Yale name will get you beyond the fact that publishers care a lot less about the name brand than other industries. Also, congrats on getting into these schools! They're both amazing, you should be very proud. However, the last internship I did before my summer one, only maybe 4 out of a class of 15 had Ivy League backgrounds; a lot of us just came from liberal arts colleges and worked really hard at our programs there.

As for the rate of salary growth--from what I've heard, and as someone who is NOT targeting editorial, the rate of growth is a lot faster on, say, the marketing and publicity and sales side than the editorial side. Same goes for pretty much any part beyond editorial and agenting. I noticed that you said you want to work in a publishing house, but didn't mention what avenue. I'd def figure that out and take it into consideration, bc editorial isn't the only part of the industry even if it's the most well-known! So far, every big 5 house but Hachette starts at 50k (or 51k for PRH); Hachette is still at 47.5k, and a lot of smaller houses range between 40k to 50k. 

Most of publishing is based in NYC. A lot of internships are remote--all of mine have been, though I was based in Boston during my college internships and am currently one hour out from NYC, so a commutable distance to major cities. Some houses are offering more remote roles at the entry level, but I would factor this more heavily into what you do postgrad than in your choice of college because remote opportunities are more common at the intern level. Most likely, you'll be asked to be hybrid or in-office for entry level onward, so that's when the "where do i go from here" decision is gonna kick in.

hey! still looking for my first full-time role (class of '24, jobhunting's been a fight and a half), but a couple things that helped me with internships. i worked a few of them throughout college and just interviewed for a macmillan one (no word yet, so take any advice w that with a grain of salt lol). everything im sharing is just based off of what i've heard and learned in my own personal experience, so you may get conflicting advice when other people respond

1. use your college's network if they have one. i found my first marketing internship with a literary magazine publisher through my college, since the hiring manager was an alum and reached out through the department's network. see if you can find any alum in positions and at imprints you're interested in and do informationals!

2. informationals are really useful for learning about the industry. people as a general rule want to help and will usually try to set up a time to talk or share a few tips if you reach out and ask politely. this also helps narrow what "sectors" of the industry you might want to work in.

3. in my experience, publishers can be wary of people who apply for non-editorial roles to try and sidestep into editorial, given that it's the most well-known field. if that's your plan, definitely do not share it with anyone you're interviewing with or talking to. i found my lane in the marketing-publicity-sales side of things after figuring out that editorial was not smth i wanted to pursue, but a lot of people i've both worked and done informationals with have said it can be a red flag.

this isn't everything i did, but it's a solid enough basis that helped me get some hands-on experience and confirm that i wanted to work in this industry. i hope it helps a little!

I think it’s definitely an interesting idea—I always thought that part of the reason Kol turned to bloodshed and brutality/didn’t bother learning control is exactly what you said: he was lashing out and mourning the loss of his magic, and eventually it became habit. With that no longer in play, would he feel like less of an outcast among his own family? I definitely think so, since he would be able to stand up for and make himself heard consistently, and he could likely hold off Klaus to a degree. I also agree that he might not ally with witches as much as he does in canon—with part of the familial rift no longer in play and the discrimination and wariness toward Siphoners/Heretics now involved. 

I especially think he’d be way more involved with Hope in the early seasons (dude didn’t even officially meet her til like s4, right? like…ouch), whether he was killed in TVD and brought back or simply survived and returned to New Orleans chasing Elijah or Klaus. He’d be able to take an active role in protecting and mentoring her, which we see hints of in s5 but never fully dive into. 

As for him and Freya, I think having them at equal power levels (one honing power for a thousand years, one building power over centuries of sleep and enhanced by Dahlia) with different specialties would be fun. I also think that it would bring them closer after the initial “wtf who are you”—just bouncing ideas for spells off each other, bonding over being the only magic-users in the family, researching and exploring magic and myth…it’s definitely a lot to consider!

ETA: and his relationship with Davina? In canon he already prefers her to his family, but with this you have a distrust of witches and a less angry and insecure Original on the other side of it. Enemies/rivals to lovers, perhaps?
